# TENDER NOTICE — KE-KCS-2026-042

**Buyer:** Kenya Customs Service · National Treasury
**Reference:** KE-KCS-2026-042
**Subject:** Supply, installation and support of container inspection scanners (drive-through X-ray) — 3 ports
**Budget ceiling:** KES 1,860,000,000 (VAT inclusive)
**Closing:** 14 February 2027, 10:00 EAT · Open international tender, two-envelope

## 1. Specifications — the Supplier SHALL:

- The supplier SHALL deliver drive-through X-ray scanners with imaging throughput of at least 25 containers/hour per site.
- The supplier SHALL complete installation and radiation-safety certification at each port within one hundred and twenty (120) days of contract signature.
- The supplier SHALL integrate scanner imagery with the existing customs risk-management system via documented API.
- The supplier SHALL train at least forty (40) customs officers as operators and fifteen (15) as image analysts.
- The supplier SHALL provide on-site spare parts for two (2) years and comprehensive maintenance for five (5) years.
- The supplier SHALL obtain type approval from the Radiation Protection Board before energising any unit.
- Bidders must supply reference installations of the same scanner model operating in at least two (2) customs administrations.
- Bidders must disclose total ionising dose per inspected container and the radiation-safety dossier.

## 2. Eligibility checklist

- [REQUIRED] Manufacturer authorization letter
- [REQUIRED] Reference installation letters (2 customs administrations)
- [REQUIRED] Radiation Protection Board type-approval dossier
- [REQUIRED] Original equipment manufacturers statement
- [REQUIRED] Tax compliance certificate

## 3. Evaluation

Scored 40% technical, 30% commercial, 30% five-year support cost of ownership. Units without RPB type approval are ineligible. Throughput guarantees below 25 containers/hour are non-responsive.

# TENDER NOTICE — KE-KEMSA-2024-ONT08

**Buyer:** Kenya Medical Supplies Authority
**Reference:** 20241003160602-206188-KEMSA/ONT08/2024-2026
**Subject:** SUPPLY OF HEALTH TECHNOLOGIES (COTTON GAUZE, COTTON WOOL &  TUBES)
**Source:** OCDS release `ocds-5whusi-KEMSA/ONT08/2024-2026`, Kenya PPRA dataset (publication 147), retrieved 2026-10-31
**Source URL:** https://data.open-contracting.org/en/publication/147

## 1. What this record is

This is a **real published award register**, not a synthetic tender pack. It is used as a
regression pack for oversight review: the desk re-reads the published record and surfaces
what a reviewer should ask about. The release carries **no tender documents, no line items
and no quantities**, so the desk cannot test unit-price reasonableness from this record.
That absence is itself a transparency gap, and the review says so.

## 2. Published awards (verbatim values)

| Supplier | Award value | Contract period |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FAMI INVESTMENT LTD | KES 2,387,988 | 2025-03-19 → 2027-03-18 |
| TENDAJI TRADING LIMITED | KES 972,400 | 2025-03-26 → 2027-03-25 |
| TOPTOUCH MARKETING LIMITED | KES 965,000 | 2025-03-13 → 2027-03-12 |
| FROTOM LOGISTICS LIMITED | KES 194,436,000 | 2025-05-20 → 2027-05-19 |
| NIFLA ENTERPRISE LIMITED | KES 52,486,248 | 2025-03-20 → 2027-03-19 |
| POWERLITE BREW AFRICA LIMITED | KES 1,453,700 | 2025-03-18 → 2027-03-17 |
| TINGLINKS ENTERPRISES LIMITED | KES 5,170,000 | 2025-03-11 → 2027-03-10 |
| ZAN GLOBAL LIMITED | KES 540,960 | 2025-03-17 → 2027-03-16 |
| VOMORONO LTD | KES 10,093,200 | 2025-03-11 → 2027-03-10 |
| MILLENIUM SOLUTIONS EAST AFRICA LIMITED | KES 69,892,200 | 2025-03-20 → 2027-03-19 |
| REMMY SUPPLIERS & SERVICES LTD | KES 4,337,800 | 2025-03-10 → 2027-03-09 |

## 3. Review questions the record supports

- The published award values span a wide range. Confirm the lot composition, quantities and
  unit prices before treating the spread as a price anomaly.
- The release does not publish the tender documents or the line items behind each award.
  A committee cannot reconstruct the evaluation from this record alone.
- Every award names a supplier; the release does not publish beneficial ownership or the
  evaluation score behind the award.

## 4. What the desk must not claim

The desk may flag the value spread and the missing record, with citations to the release.
It must not conclude that any supplier overcharged, that any award is improper, or that the
release proves fraud. Those are questions for the committee, backed by the documents the
release does not contain.

# TENDER NOTICE — RW-UMUCYO-2027-006

**Buyer:** Rwanda Biomedical Centre · Umucyo e-procurement
**Reference:** RW-UMUCYO-2027-006
**Subject:** Community health worker digital kits — solar tablets, diagnostics and connectivity (7,500 kits)
**Budget ceiling:** RWF 9,800,000,000 (VAT inclusive)
**Closing:** 03 March 2027, 09:00 CAT · Framework agreement, open to prequalified suppliers

## 1. Specifications — the Supplier SHALL:

- The supplier SHALL deliver solar tablets rated for a minimum of 8 hours continuous field use per charge.
- The supplier SHALL preload the national community-health application and verify boot integrity on every unit.
- The supplier SHALL supply rapid diagnostic test (RDT) cassettes WHO-prequalified for malaria and pneumonia.
- The supplier SHALL enable remote device management with firmware updates signed by the buyer.
- The supplier SHALL replace defective units within ten (10) working days under the framework.
- Suppliers must maintain a repair depot in-country with certified technicians.
- Bidders must guarantee connectivity bundles (SMS + data) for three (3) years.
- Bidders must declare the country of final assembly for all hardware.

## 2. Eligibility checklist

- [REQUIRED] In-country repair depot certificate
- [REQUIRED] WHO prequalification certificates for RDTs
- [REQUIRED] Connectivity bundle guarantee (3 years)
- [REQUIRED] Tax clearance (RRA) certificate

## 3. Evaluation

Framework awarded per lot: tablets, RDTs, connectivity. Evaluated on unit price, support load and five-year connectivity cost. Devices without signed firmware are non-responsive.
